findings.F1: The block result rests on a few outliers: the 499 active blocks have mean 0.340, median -0.178, std 6.08 and max 77.5; the top 10 blocks hold 183% of the total; after a 1% winsorisation t falls from 1.25 to 0.60; and dropping the top 5 blocks turns the mean negative (-0.122, t -0.74), with only 37% of blocks positive.
findings.F2: Within forecast>0 bars, the effect splits by recent momentum: when the close is up over the past 20 bars, the 20-bar excess return is +0.035 (t 6.66, hit 45.7%, n 3856), and when it is down it is -0.027 (t -5.93, hit 37.5%, n 3190); the t-values use overlapping bars, so they are overstated.
findings.F3: The same split appears with the distance to the SMA: when the distance has risen over the last 10 bars, excess is +0.039 (t 6.93, hit 46.5%, n 3494), and when it has fallen it is -0.025 (t -5.72, hit 37.6%, n 3552).
findings.F4: Time since the cross works against the brief's "new trend" reading: the first 10 bars above the SMA give -0.011 (t -1.96, n 1953) and bars 10-30 give -0.002 (t -0.27), while bars 30-60 give +0.016 (t 2.40) and bars 60-120 give +0.035 (t 4.57).
findings.F5: The market regime decides the sign: when BTC is also above its 200-day SMA, active bars give +0.013 (t 3.51, n 6264), and when BTC is below it they give -0.049 (t -5.88, hit 38.0%, n 782).
findings.F6: The effect depends on the period: active blocks lost in 2018 (mean -1.92, t -3.33) and 2022 (-0.60, t -2.01) and were positive but not significant in 2020, 2024 and 2025 (t 1.31, 1.33, 1.07); bar-level hit rates were only 17-18% in 2018 and 2022, against 54% in 2020.
findings.F7: Across coins the block result is uneven and nowhere significant: BTC t 1.42, ZEC mean 1.64 with t 1.18, and ETH, LTC and XMR near zero or negative (t -0.18, 0.11, -0.49); without ZEC the pooled block t falls to 0.53.
findings.F8: The forecast's grading is only weakly tied to outcomes: excess is negative in the two lowest forecast quintiles (-0.027, -0.023) and positive in the top three (+0.016, +0.015, +0.052), but medians are negative in every quintile (-0.022 to -0.044) and the hit rate stays at 39-45%; by raw distance, the farthest quintile (mean 110% above the SMA) turns negative again (-0.014, median -0.056).
findings.F9: The positive means come from right-skewed returns, not from frequent wins: active bars have mean excess +0.0065 against +0.0002 for inactive bars, yet only 42.0% of active bars beat the coin's drift, so most of the time the position is drowned by the coin's own moves.

ideas.idea: When a coin's daily close is above its 200-day SMA and also higher than it was 20 bars earlier, its return over the next 20 bars beats its own average drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader would take the above-average long only when the coin's 20-bar momentum is also up, and refuse it when the coin has been falling while still above the average.
ideas.name: Above average with rising momentum

ideas.idea: When a coin's close is above its 200-day SMA and its percent distance above the SMA is larger than it was 10 bars earlier, its return over the next 20 bars beats its own average drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold the long only while the gap above the average is widening, and stand aside when the gap is shrinking.
ideas.name: Widening gap above average

ideas.idea: When a coin's close has stayed above its 200-day SMA for at least 30 consecutive bars, its return over the next 20 bars beats its own average drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader would treat a close above the average as a long only once that trend has lasted, not right after the cross.
ideas.name: Established stay above average
